actions: Revalidated clean control tuple with SHA-only Git-ref lookups before semantic work.
Continued the own long-horizon frontier from the Repo2Skill-Evo maintenance checkpoint.
Researched public primary/current sources on contract-triggered skill drift, paired skill-value measurement, continual skill maintenance, affected-set replay, and governed release/rollback.
Primary-source checked OpenLoopEvolve release semantics, trigger role, YC-Bench outcomes, and evolution-validation token cost.
Separated observed evidence from a new value-weighted maintenance-scheduler hypothesis and retained explicit scope guards.
Persisted and read back a new role-local checkpoint and advanced the role-local LATEST pointer.
new_evidence_summary: Operational drift hazard and current marginal skill value are empirically distinct signals.
Explicit skill maintenance can fail to outperform pure retained-context adaptation on average, so not every stored skill merits maintenance spend.
Relevant-history replay and relation graphs support blast-radius-bounded verification but do not establish a cost-optimal replay set.

Champion-Challenger release with benefit/evidence/tail-risk/resource-cost constraints plus task-boundary activation and rollback is supported on YC-Bench, but incurs material evolution-validation cost.

A value-weighted maintenance priority combining invalidation probability, marginal lift, consequence, maintenance cost and false-edit risk remains a synthesis hypothesis, not an established end-to-end result.

termination.cause: current runtime boundary after a substantive checkpoint iteration

exact_next_action: Inspect the official OpenLoopEvolve code/config for concrete Trig and CanaryMonitor thresholds and threshold ablations; then search for controlled software/API-agent studies that jointly vary drift hazard, marginal skill value, maintenance cost, and false-edit/tail risk while continuing Repo2Skill-Evo artifact and common-replicate admission×maintenance factorial searches.
